Undergraduate Academic Regulations 2026
Page 1
 NORTHBRIDGE INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY
 Office of Academic Affairs
 UNDERGRADUATE ACADEMIC REGULATIONS 2026
Document code: NIT/AA/UGR/2026
Version: 1.0
Effective from: 1 August 2026
Classification: Academic policy - approved for student reference
1. Purpose and application
1.1 These regulations govern undergraduate programmes offered by Northbridge Institute of Technology from the
academic year 2026-27. They apply to students admitted in 2026 and to later cohorts unless a subsequent
regulation expressly provides otherwise.
1.2 The regulations set minimum academic requirements for registration, credit completion, progression,
assessment, project work and graduation. Programme-specific curriculum documents may impose additional
requirements but shall not reduce the standards stated here.
1.3 Questions concerning interpretation shall be referred to the Office of Academic Affairs. A department may issue
implementation instructions only when those instructions are consistent with these regulations.
2. Definitions
 a. Academic year means the period beginning with the Autumn semester and ending after the following Summer
 term.
b. Credit means the academic value assigned to a course according to its scheduled learning hours and assessed
 work.
c. Registered course means a course entered in the official student registration record for a semester.
 d. Backlog means a required course in which the student has not yet earned a passing grade.
 e. CGPA means the cumulative grade point average calculated from all credit-bearing courses completed at the
 Institute.
3. Academic structure
3.1 Each academic year normally consists of an Autumn semester, a Spring semester and an optional Summer
term. The detailed teaching, registration and examination dates are published separately in the academic calendar.
3.2 A regular semester shall normally include at least fifteen weeks of instruction, excluding the end-semester
examination period. The Summer term may be used for repeat courses, approved electives, internships or other
academic activities.
3.3 Courses may be classified as institute core, programme core, programme elective, open elective, laboratory,
project, seminar or internship. The approved curriculum shall state the classification and credit value of each course.
4. Semester registration
4.1 A student must complete registration within the period announced in the academic calendar. Registration is valid
only after academic advising, selection of permitted courses and clearance of applicable institutional holds.
4.2 The normal semester load is 18 to 24 credits. A student may register for up to 27 credits with the written
recommendation of the faculty adviser and approval of the Head of Department.
4.3 A student with a CGPA below 5.00 shall normally be restricted to a maximum of 20 credits in the following
regular semester so that failed and essential prerequisite courses can be given priority.
4.4 Late registration may be permitted for up to five working days after the published deadline upon payment of the
prescribed late fee. Registration after this period requires approval from the Dean of Academic Affairs and shall be
allowed only for documented reasons.

5. Course prerequisites and changes
5.1 A student shall not register for a course without completing every prerequisite stated in the approved curriculum.
Concurrent registration may be allowed only when the curriculum explicitly identifies the courses as co-requisites.
5.2 The add and drop period shall close at the end of the second week of instruction. A course dropped within this
period will not appear as an attempted course in the semester grade report.
5.3 Withdrawal after the add and drop period may be approved up to the end of the eighth week. An approved
withdrawal shall be recorded with the grade W and shall not contribute to the SGPA or CGPA.
5.4 A compulsory course may not be withdrawn if withdrawal would prevent the student from meeting a prerequisite
required for progression in the following semester.
6. Assessment and grading
6.1 Course assessment may include quizzes, assignments, laboratory work, projects, mid-semester examinations
and end-semester examinations. The course outline issued at the beginning of the semester shall state the
assessment components and their weightages.
6.2 The Institute uses letter grades O, A+, A, B+, B, C, P and F for credit-bearing courses. The grade P is the
minimum passing grade. Non-credit requirements may be recorded as Satisfactory or Unsatisfactory.
6.3 A student receiving the grade F must repeat the course when it is compulsory. An elective failed with grade F
may be repeated or replaced by another approved elective, subject to curriculum requirements.
6.4 The semester grade point average is calculated using courses registered in that semester. The cumulative grade
point average is calculated using all completed credit-bearing courses, subject to the Institute's approved
grade-replacement rules.
7. Academic progression
7.1 A student is in good academic standing when the CGPA is at least 5.00 and the student is not subject to
suspension under these regulations.
7.2 A student whose CGPA falls below 5.00 shall be placed on academic warning for the next regular semester. The
student must meet the faculty adviser and follow the approved reduced-load study plan.
7.3 A student may progress to the third year only after earning at least 70 credits. Progression to the fourth year
requires at least 108 earned credits and no more than four active backlogs.
7.4 A student who fails to earn at least 40 credits during any two consecutive regular academic years may be
considered for academic suspension after review by the Institute Academic Committee.
7.5 Before suspension is imposed, the student shall be given an opportunity to submit documented circumstances
and an academic recovery plan. The final decision shall be communicated in writing.
8. Repeating courses and grade improvement
8.1 A failed compulsory course shall be repeated at the earliest available offering, subject to timetable feasibility and
prerequisite sequencing.
8.2 A student may repeat a passed course for grade improvement only once and only when the original grade is C or
P. No more than two grade-improvement courses may be registered in a single semester.
8.3 Both attempts shall remain visible on the transcript. The better grade shall be used for CGPA calculation, but the
academic record shall retain the complete attempt history.

9. Internship, project and seminar requirements
9.1 Every student must complete the internship requirement stated in the approved programme curriculum. An
internship shall be evaluated only when it has prior departmental approval and the required report and supervisor
assessment are submitted.
9.2 Registration for the final-year project requires at least 108 earned credits and completion of every project
prerequisite listed by the department.
9.3 The project may be carried out individually or in an approved group. Each student remains responsible for
demonstrating an identifiable contribution during review and final evaluation.
9.4 Where a programme includes a seminar or comprehensive review, successful completion is required before the
final degree audit.
10. Graduation requirements
10.1 To qualify for the award of an undergraduate degree, a student must complete at least 160 credits and every
compulsory non-credit requirement prescribed by the programme.
10.2 The student must obtain a final CGPA of at least 5.00, clear all compulsory courses, complete the internship
and project requirements, and have no pending disciplinary penalty that prevents the award of the degree.
10.3 The normal duration of the programme is four academic years. All degree requirements must be completed
within a maximum of seven academic years from the date of first registration, excluding formally approved breaks in
study.
10.4 The Office of Academic Affairs shall conduct a degree audit after final results are published. Meeting the credit
total alone does not establish graduation eligibility when a compulsory course or non-credit requirement remains
incomplete.
11. Break in study and readmission
11.1 A student may apply for a temporary break in study on medical, financial or other serious grounds. The request
should ordinarily be submitted before the semester registration deadline and must include supporting documents.
11.2 A break may be approved for one semester at a time and shall normally not exceed two consecutive semesters.
The approved period will not be counted toward active semesters but remains subject to the maximum programme
duration in clause 10.3 unless specifically exempted.
11.3 Readmission requires confirmation of the curriculum and regulations applicable on return. Where the curriculum
has changed, the department may prescribe equivalent or bridge courses.
12. Academic records and appeals
12.1 Students are responsible for checking their registration record, grade report and earned-credit summary. Any
discrepancy should be reported to the appropriate office within the period stated in the relevant notice.
12.2 An appeal concerning the application of these regulations must be submitted to the Dean of Academic Affairs
within ten working days of the communicated decision. The appeal must identify the disputed clause and provide
supporting material.
12.3 An appeal does not automatically suspend an academic decision. Interim relief may be granted only through a
written direction of the Dean or the Institute Academic Committee.
13. Authority and commencement
13.1 These regulations were approved by the Institute Academic Council on 10 June 2026 and take effect on 1
August 2026.
13.2 The Institute may issue amendments through a formally numbered notification. Where an amendment conflicts
with this document, the later effective provision shall apply.
Issued by:
Dean of Academic Affairs
Northbridge Institute of Technology

report and admission or readmission order within five working days of publication of the updated record.

equal credit values do not establish equivalence without an approved mapping.

Page 1
 NORTHBRIDGE INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY
 Office of Academic Affairs
 UNDERGRADUATE ATTENDANCE POLICY 2026
Document code: NIT/AA/ATT/2026
Version: 2.0
Effective from: 1 August 2026
Classification: Academic policy - approved for student reference
1. Purpose
1.1 Regular participation in scheduled academic work is an essential part of every undergraduate course. This policy
establishes the minimum attendance requirement, the method of calculation and the procedure to be followed when
attendance is below the prescribed level.
1.2 The policy applies to lectures, tutorials, laboratories, studios, workshops, seminars and other scheduled course
activities for undergraduate programmes offered by Northbridge Institute of Technology.
1.3 This policy should be read with the examination regulations and any formally issued attendance-relaxation
notification. A later notification applies only to the extent expressly stated in that notification.
2. Minimum attendance requirement
2.1 A student must maintain at least 75 percent attendance in each registered course to be eligible to appear in the
end-semester examination or final course assessment.
2.2 Attendance is assessed separately for every course. A high overall semester attendance percentage does not
compensate for attendance below 75 percent in an individual course.
2.3 For a course without an end-semester examination, the same minimum applies to eligibility for the final practical,
presentation, jury, viva or other concluding assessment.
2.4 A department may prescribe a higher attendance requirement for a clinical, field-based, safety-critical or
professionally regulated course when the higher requirement is stated in the approved course outline before
registration.
3. Calculation of attendance
3.1 Attendance percentage is calculated as the number of attended scheduled sessions divided by the number of
sessions conducted, multiplied by 100.
3.2 A session cancelled by the Institute or rescheduled without adequate notice shall not be counted as a conducted
session. A rescheduled session counts when it is announced through the official timetable or learning system.
3.3 Attendance records shall be maintained by the course instructor and updated at least once every seven calendar
days. Students should review their records regularly and report possible errors promptly.
3.4 For combined lecture and laboratory courses, the department may calculate attendance separately for each
component when the approved course outline states separate requirements.
4. Recording attendance
4.1 Attendance may be recorded through the Institute attendance system, a signed register or another method
approved by the department. The instructor remains responsible for verifying the final record.
4.2 A student arriving more than fifteen minutes after the scheduled start may be marked absent unless the
instructor accepts a documented academic or emergency reason.
4.3 Leaving a session before its completion without permission may be treated as absence. Attendance obtained
through impersonation, proxy marking or manipulation of records constitutes misconduct.

5. Absence for approved activities
5.1 Participation in an Institute-approved academic, cultural or sports activity does not automatically count as
attendance. The student must obtain activity approval and submit it to the department within three working days after
returning.
5.2 The department may grant attendance credit for approved representation of the Institute when the student has
completed any alternative work prescribed by the course instructor.
5.3 Travel days may be considered only when included in the approved activity schedule. Personal travel and
preparation time are not eligible for attendance credit.
6. Medical and emergency absence
6.1 A medical certificate explains an absence but does not automatically convert the missed session into
attendance. Medical circumstances are considered through the attendance-relaxation procedure.
6.2 Medical documents should be issued by a registered medical practitioner and should state the period during
which the student was unable to attend academic activities.
6.3 A student should submit medical or emergency documents within five working days of returning to classes.
Delayed submission may be accepted when the delay itself is supported by documented circumstances.
7. Attendance warnings
7.1 The attendance system shall provide an advisory warning when attendance in a course falls below 80 percent.
The warning is intended to allow corrective action and does not change the minimum eligibility requirement.
7.2 A student receiving a warning should meet the course instructor or faculty adviser and review the number of
remaining scheduled sessions.
7.3 Failure to receive an automated warning does not remove the student's responsibility to maintain the required
attendance.
8. Shortage and examination eligibility
8.1 After the final instructional session, each department shall prepare the course-wise attendance list. A student
with attendance of 75 percent or above shall be marked eligible, subject to other examination requirements.
8.2 A student below 75 percent shall be marked provisionally ineligible until any permitted relaxation application is
decided.
8.3 A student with attendance below 65 percent in a course is not eligible for attendance relaxation under the
ordinary medical or emergency procedure and must repeat the course when next offered, unless a separate
exceptional order applies.
8.4 Attendance from 65 percent to 74 percent may be considered for relaxation only under the separate
Undergraduate Attendance Relaxation Guidelines and does not create an automatic entitlement.
9. Correction of attendance records
9.1 A student who believes an attendance entry is incorrect must submit a correction request to the course instructor
within five working days of the record being published.
9.2 The request must identify the course, date and session concerned. Supporting evidence may include a signed
laboratory record, assessment submission or official activity approval.
9.3 If the matter is not resolved by the instructor, the student may refer it to the Head of Department within three
further working days. The decision shall be based on the available institutional record.

10. Responsibilities
10.1 Students are responsible for attending scheduled sessions, checking published attendance and reporting
discrepancies within the prescribed time.
10.2 Course instructors are responsible for maintaining accurate records, publishing updates regularly and
responding to correction requests.
10.3 Departments are responsible for monitoring the publication of attendance, reviewing unresolved discrepancies
and issuing the final eligibility list.
10.4 The Office of Academic Affairs is responsible for maintaining this policy, issuing clarification where required and
coordinating any Institute-wide amendments.
11. Special course arrangements
11.1 For internships, projects and field courses where attendance cannot be recorded by ordinary class sessions,
the department shall define participation requirements before registration.
11.2 Online or blended sessions count toward attendance when they are included in the official course schedule.
The instructor may use authenticated participation records, required activities or another announced method to verify
attendance.
11.3 Attendance requirements for make-up classes shall be the same as for regular sessions when the make-up
schedule is announced at least twenty-four hours in advance, except in an emergency closure.
12. Misconduct and falsification
12.1 Creating a false attendance record, marking attendance for another student, altering an attendance document
or submitting a fabricated medical certificate may be referred for disciplinary action.
12.2 Correction of a genuine administrative error is not misconduct. No adverse finding shall be made without giving
the student an opportunity to respond.
12.3 Where a suspected falsification affects examination eligibility, the department may place the decision on hold
until the preliminary verification is completed.
13. Appeals
13.1 An appeal against the final course attendance percentage must first be submitted to the Head of Department
within three working days of publication of the eligibility list.
13.2 A further appeal may be submitted to the Dean of Academic Affairs within five working days of the departmental
decision. The appeal must identify the disputed sessions and include all available supporting material.
13.3 An appeal based only on a request to waive the minimum percentage, without a permitted ground under the
relaxation guidelines, shall not be considered as an attendance-record appeal.
14. Records and retention
14.1 Course attendance records and approved corrections shall be retained for at least one academic year after
publication of the final result for the course.
14.2 Medical documents and relaxation decisions shall be handled as restricted student records and accessed only
for the stated academic purpose.
15. Commencement and supersession
15.1 This policy takes effect on 1 August 2026 and supersedes the Undergraduate Attendance Policy 2025 for
students and courses covered by this document.
15.2 The previous general minimum of 70 percent shall not apply to courses beginning on or after the effective date
of this policy.
15.3 Any amendment must be issued through a numbered notification approved by the Institute Academic Council or
another authority formally delegated for that purpose.

Attendance Relaxation Guidelines 2026
Page 1
 NORTHBRIDGE INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY
 Office of Academic Affairs
UNDERGRADUATE ATTENDANCE RELAXATION GUIDELINES
 2026
Document code: NIT/AA/ARL/2026
Version: 1.0
Effective from: 1 August 2026
Classification: Academic policy - approved for student reference
1. Purpose and relationship to the attendance policy
1.1 These guidelines establish the limited circumstances in which an undergraduate student with attendance below the
ordinary minimum may request relaxation for a particular course.
1.2 The ordinary requirement remains 75 percent attendance in each registered course under the Undergraduate
Attendance Policy 2026. Relaxation is an exception considered on documented grounds and is not an automatic
entitlement.
1.3 These guidelines apply separately to every affected course. Approval in one course does not establish eligibility in
another course.
2. Basic eligibility
2.1 A student may apply when final attendance in the affected course is between 65 percent and 74 percent, inclusive.
2.2 A student whose attendance is below 65 percent is ordinarily not eligible under these guidelines and must repeat the
course when it is next offered.
2.3 An application may be considered only when the shortage is connected to one or more permitted grounds stated in
section 3 and the student has supplied reasonable supporting evidence.
2.4 The student must have completed the essential laboratory, studio, clinical or field components identified by the
department. Relaxation shall not be used to waive a compulsory practical requirement.
3. Permitted grounds
 a. Illness, hospitalization, injury or a medically advised period of rest supported by records from a registered medical
 practitioner.
b. A serious family emergency, bereavement or another exceptional personal circumstance supported by appropriate
 documents.
c. Official representation of the Institute in an approved academic, cultural or sports activity when attendance credit
 could not reasonably be granted under the ordinary policy.
d. Disruption caused by a documented public emergency, natural event or transport closure affecting the student's
 ability to attend.
e. An established administrative or timetable error that cannot be fully corrected through the ordinary
 attendance-record correction process.
4. Grounds normally not accepted
 a. Personal travel, vacations, social events or employment undertaken without prior academic approval.
 b. Preparation for another course, examination, competition or private certification.
 c. Failure to monitor published attendance or reliance on an estimated attendance percentage.
 d. A general request for leniency without documents or a specific explanation of the affected period.
 5. Application deadline
5.1 The completed application must reach the department at least seven working days before the first scheduled
end-semester examination for the programme.
5.2 When the shortage arises or becomes known after that deadline, the application must be submitted within two
working days of the relevant event or publication of the final attendance record.
5.3 A delayed application may be accepted only when the student demonstrates that timely submission was not
reasonably possible.

6. Application procedure
6.1 The student shall submit Form ATT-07 separately for each course in which relaxation is requested. The form must
state the course code, recorded attendance, period of absence and ground relied upon.
6.2 The application shall first be submitted to the faculty adviser, who will check completeness and forward it to the
course instructor and Head of Department.
6.3 The student should retain a copy or electronic acknowledgement showing the date of submission. Submission alone
does not permit the student to appear in the examination.
7. Supporting documents
7.1 Medical applications should include a certificate stating the relevant period and, where available, consultation,
admission or discharge records. A diagnosis need not be disclosed beyond what is necessary to establish inability to
attend.
7.2 Applications based on Institute representation must include the approval issued by the responsible faculty member
or office and the confirmed activity schedule.
7.3 For a family emergency or public disruption, the committee may accept official notices, travel interruption records,
declarations or other material appropriate to the circumstances.
7.4 The Institute may verify a submitted document with the issuing organization. Fabricated or altered evidence may be
referred for disciplinary action.
8. Departmental verification
8.1 The course instructor shall confirm the number of sessions conducted, the student's recorded attendance and
whether essential assessed activities were completed.
8.2 The Head of Department shall confirm that any attendance correction request has been resolved before the
relaxation application is considered.
8.3 Where records are incomplete, the department shall make reasonable efforts to verify them. Uncertainty created
solely by an institutional recording failure shall not be held against the student.
9. Attendance Relaxation Committee
9.1 Each school shall constitute an Attendance Relaxation Committee consisting of the Head of School or nominee, one
senior faculty member and an Academic Affairs representative.
9.2 A member directly involved in a disputed record should disclose that involvement and may provide information but
shall not determine the application alone.
9.3 The committee may approve, reject or seek limited additional information. Decisions must be based on the
applicable percentage, the permitted ground, supporting evidence and completion of essential course work.
10. Decision standards
10.1 Attendance between 70 percent and 74 percent may be relaxed where a permitted ground is supported and
essential course requirements have been completed.
10.2 Attendance between 65 percent and 69 percent requires evidence of serious circumstances and a specific
recommendation from the Head of Department.
10.3 No relaxation may increase the recorded attendance percentage. Approval only changes examination eligibility for
the stated course and semester.
10.4 The committee shall apply comparable standards to comparable cases while considering the individual duration
and effect of the documented circumstances.

11. Communication and examination status
11.1 The decision shall identify the student, course, recorded percentage, outcome and any condition attached to
approval. Reasons should be stated briefly when an application is rejected.
11.2 The department shall communicate the decision through the official student communication channel and update
the examination eligibility record.
11.3 When a decision remains pending on the examination date, provisional appearance may be authorized only in
writing by the Dean of Academic Affairs. The answer script shall not be evaluated if the application is later rejected,
unless an appeal changes the outcome.
12. Conditions attached to approval
12.1 The committee may require completion of missed laboratory work, an additional academic task or another
reasonable activity directly connected to the missed instruction.
12.2 Any condition must be stated in the written decision with a completion date. Failure to satisfy the condition may
result in withdrawal of the relaxation before result processing.
12.3 A fee, donation or unrelated service requirement shall not be imposed as a condition of attendance relaxation.
13. Appeal
13.1 A student may appeal a rejection to the Dean of Academic Affairs within three working days of receiving the
decision.
13.2 The appeal must identify a material error in the attendance record, application of the eligibility range, consideration
of evidence or procedure followed by the committee.
13.3 New evidence may be considered when the student explains why it was not reasonably available with the original
application.
13.4 The Dean's decision shall be final for the semester, without limiting correction of a later-discovered institutional
record error.
14. Records, privacy and reporting
14.1 Applications and decisions shall be retained as restricted academic records for at least one academic year after
publication of the relevant course result.
14.2 Medical and personal documents shall be accessed only by staff involved in verification, decision or appeal and
shall not be reproduced in general departmental reports.
14.3 Academic Affairs may prepare anonymized statistics showing the number of applications, percentage ranges,
outcomes and grounds for policy review.
15. Commencement
15.1 These guidelines take effect on 1 August 2026 and apply to courses beginning on or after that date.
15.2 They shall be reviewed after the 2026-27 academic year. Any amendment must be issued through a numbered
notification.

Page 1

 MANDATORY INTERNSHIP GUIDELINES 2026
Document code: NIT/CDIR/INT/2026
Version: Version 1.0
Effective from: 1 August 2026
Classification: Academic and industry engagement policy - approved for student reference
1. Purpose and Scope
1.1 These guidelines govern the mandatory undergraduate industry internship at Northbridge Institute of Technology.
They apply to Institute-facilitated and independently arranged internships used to satisfy a programme curriculum
requirement.
1.2 The internship is an academic component. Employment, stipend, accommodation or a later job offer is not
guaranteed by registration or Institute approval.
2. Academic Requirement
2.1 The B.Tech Computer Science and Engineering curriculum records the internship as CS491 Industry Internship
carrying four credits.
2.2 The approved internship must include at least six weeks of supervised work. The six weeks may be continuous or
divided into no more than two approved periods with the same host organisation.
2.3 An internship shorter than six weeks, including one ended early by the student or host, does not satisfy the
requirement unless the department approves additional supervised work.
2.4 An internship may be on-site, hybrid or remote. The department must be able to verify supervision, working dates,
assigned tasks and student participation.
3. Eligibility
3.1 Students normally undertake the internship after completing Semester VI. A department may approve an earlier
period when the student has completed the supporting courses needed for the proposed work.
3.2 The student must be registered in the relevant programme, must not be under an active disciplinary suspension and
must have no unresolved restriction that prevents participation at the host site.
3.3 Academic eligibility does not override a host organisation's lawful selection, safety, confidentiality or technical
requirements.
4. Calendar and Deadlines
 15 March 2027 - Last date to submit a request for an independently arranged Summer 2027 host organisation.
 30 April 2027 - Deadline for departmental approval of the host, faculty coordinator and learning plan.
 31 May-30 July 2027 - Recommended Summer internship period. Any approved six-week period within or overlapping
 these dates may be used.
13 August 2027 - Deadline for the internship report, host evaluation and completion evidence for Summer 2027.
 4.1 A department may publish an earlier internal deadline. A later date applies only when an official Institute or
departmental notice identifies the affected internship cycle.
5. Approval Before Joining
5.1 The student must submit the host name and address, supervisor contact, proposed dates, work area, work mode
and a brief learning plan.
5.2 The department verifies academic relevance and appoints a faculty coordinator. Career Development and Industry
Relations may verify the organisation and placement terms.
5.3 Work completed before written approval is not automatically eligible for credit. Retrospective approval is limited to
documented administrative error and requires the Head of Department's recommendation.

6. Host and Supervision Requirements
6.1 The host must assign a supervisor who can confirm attendance, assigned work, conduct and performance. A
student may not act as their own supervisor or use an organisation they control without additional departmental
oversight.
6.2 The faculty coordinator maintains periodic contact and may request progress records, a virtual review or a site visit.
6.3 The host must provide a reasonably safe working environment and communicate applicable workplace,
information-security and confidentiality rules.
7. Student Responsibilities
 a. Attend according to the approved schedule and maintain a weekly activity log.
 b. Follow host safety, confidentiality, data-protection and acceptable-use requirements.
 c. Inform the host supervisor and faculty coordinator promptly about absence, serious difficulty or a proposed change
 in work.
d. Use only authorised data, systems, software and equipment.
 e. Submit original academic work and clearly identify confidential material that cannot appear in the report.
 7.1 The student must complete at least 90 percent of scheduled working days. An absence exceeding three working
days normally requires an approved extension so that the six-week requirement is met.
8. Change, Interruption and Withdrawal
8.1 A student may not change the host, work mode or approved dates without written permission from the faculty
coordinator.
8.2 If a host ends the internship for reasons not caused by student misconduct, the department may approve transfer to
another host and combine verified periods.
8.3 If the student withdraws or is removed for misconduct, the department determines whether completed work can be
evaluated. Serious misconduct may be referred under Institute disciplinary rules.
9. Required Evidence
 a. Joining confirmation or host appointment letter.
 b. Weekly activity log approved by the host supervisor.
 c. Host completion certificate showing actual start and end dates.
 d. Host supervisor evaluation in the prescribed format.
 e. Student report and presentation or oral examination.
 9.1 A certificate alone is not sufficient for academic credit when the report, evaluation or required review is missing.
10. Report Requirements
10.1 The report must describe the organisation, assigned problem, work completed, methods or tools used, results,
learning outcomes and limitations.
10.2 Confidential details may be replaced by a technical summary approved by the host. Confidentiality does not
remove the requirement to demonstrate substantial work.

1. Purpose and Application
1.1 This policy states the Institute-level conditions for student participation in campus recruitment,
internship-to-placement conversion and pre-placement offer processes.
1.2 Campus placement is a facilitation service. Registration, eligibility or participation does not guarantee an interview,
selection or employment offer.
1.3 An employer may impose stricter academic, skill, citizenship, location, medical or programme criteria. The
employer's published criteria apply in addition to this policy.
2. General Eligibility
2.1 A student must be enrolled full-time in an eligible programme and year group announced for the recruitment cycle.
2.2 A final-year undergraduate student must normally have earned at least 108 credits before the placement registration
date.
2.3 A student with more than two active backlogs is not eligible for campus placement. An active backlog is a course
with an F grade or another result requiring completion.
2.4 The minimum Institute CGPA for general participation is 6.00. An employer may require a higher CGPA or specified
marks in earlier examinations.
2.5 The student must have no active disciplinary suspension and no unresolved finding of examination misconduct that
restricts participation.
3. Academic Record Date
3.1 Eligibility is checked using results officially recorded at 5:00 p.m. on the closing date stated for a drive. A pending
examination, supplementary registration or re-evaluation request does not count as a pass.
3.2 A later grade change affects only drives whose registration remains open, unless the employer and Training and
Placement Office approve reconsideration.
3.3 The student must report a material record change promptly. Portal access created by an outdated result does not
establish eligibility.
4. Placement Registration
4.1 Students must register through the placement portal, accept the participation declaration and upload the required
resume and academic information by the cycle deadline.
4.2 The resume must use verifiable information. Qualifications, grades, projects, internships, employment and
achievements may be checked against supporting records.
4.3 A student who does not intend to participate should not register for a drive. Repeated absence after registration may
result in temporary restriction under Section 9.
5. Company-Specific Screening
5.1 The Training and Placement Office publishes the employer's programme, graduation year, CGPA, backlog, skill and
other stated criteria before registration closes.
5.2 Where employer criteria are ambiguous, the Office seeks written clarification. Students should not rely on informal
statements from peers, alumni or employees.
5.3 The employer controls shortlisting and selection. The Institute does not alter assessment scores or require an
employer to interview every Institute-eligible student.

6.1 A pre-placement offer received after an approved internship must be reported to the Training and Placement Office
within three working days.
6.2 A verified and accepted pre-placement offer is treated as an employment offer for subsequent placement
participation. Conditional offers remain subject to the conditions stated by the employer.
6.3 The internship grade and academic credits are determined independently under the Mandatory Internship
Guidelines 2026.
7. Offer Categories and Further Participation
7.1 The Office may classify opportunities as regular or higher opportunity before registration, using criteria announced
for the placement cycle.
7.2 After accepting a regular offer, a student may participate only in opportunities formally identified as higher
opportunities. After accepting a higher opportunity, the student exits further campus placement unless an exceptional
drive states otherwise.
7.3 A student may not hold two accepted campus offers at the same time. Acceptance of a permitted later offer requires
written release from the earlier campus process.

8.1 A registered student must attend scheduled tests, interviews, briefings and document-verification sessions or
withdraw before the published cut-off.
8.2 An absence caused by examination, medical emergency or another documented serious reason must be reported
as soon as practicable. The employer decides whether rescheduling is available.
8.3 Students must maintain at least 75 percent attendance in mandatory placement-readiness sessions announced for
their cohort. An approved academic attendance relaxation does not automatically excuse a placement session.
9. Missed Activities and Temporary Restriction
9.1 A student who misses a registered drive without timely withdrawal or accepted reason receives a written warning for
the first occurrence.
9.2 A second unexcused occurrence may result in restriction from the next two campus drives. A third may result in
removal from the remaining cycle after review by the Placement Committee.
9.3 A restriction applies to Institute-facilitated drives and does not prevent the student from seeking employment
independently.

10.1 Students must follow examination-style integrity during employer assessments and professional conduct during
communication, interviews and visits.
10.2 Impersonation, unauthorised assistance, false documents, manipulated grades or deliberate misrepresentation
results in immediate suspension from placement activity pending review.

without permission.

1. Programme Overview
1.1 The Bachelor of Technology in Computer Science and Engineering is a four-year undergraduate programme
organised over eight semesters. The curriculum combines computing foundations, systems, software development,
mathematical preparation, electives, internship and project work.
1.2 A student must earn at least 160 credits and satisfy all academic regulations to qualify for the degree. The normal
duration is four years and the maximum permitted duration is seven years from initial registration.
2. Credit Structure
 a. Computer science core courses and laboratories: 74 credits.
 b. Mathematics, basic sciences, engineering and humanities: 34 credits.
 c. Programme electives: 18 credits.
 d. Open electives: 14 credits.
 e. Internship and project work: 20 credits.
 2.1 The semester plan carries 20 credits in each semester, for a programme total of 160 credits. Approved substitutions
must preserve the applicable category and total credit requirement.

12. Electives
12.1 Programme electives provide advanced study within computing. The department announces the available list
before registration. An elective is offered only when staffing, facilities and minimum enrolment requirements are met.
12.2 Indicative programme electives include Data Mining, Distributed Systems, Computer Vision, Advanced Databases,
Mobile Computing, DevOps Engineering, Cryptography and Human-Computer Interaction.
12.3 Open electives may be selected from approved offerings outside the home programme. A course already counted
toward another curriculum category cannot be counted again as an open elective.
13. Internship and Project Work
13.1 CS491 requires an approved internship of at least six weeks. Students must obtain departmental approval before
joining the host organisation and must submit a report and supervisor assessment after completion.
13.2 Project Phase I covers problem definition, literature review, requirements, method selection and an initial
implementation. Project Phase II continues the approved work and concludes with a dissertation, demonstration and
oral examination.
13.3 Registration for final-year project work normally requires at least 108 earned credits and no more than four active
backlogs. The department may require completion of specific supporting courses for a proposed topic.
14. Progression and Degree Requirements
14.1 Progression to the third year normally requires at least 70 earned credits. Progression to the fourth year normally
requires at least 108 earned credits and no more than four active backlogs.
14.2 For graduation, a student must earn 160 credits, complete all compulsory components, achieve a CGPA of at least
5.00 and clear all outstanding academic or disciplinary requirements.
14.3 Failure in a course does not remove its prerequisite effect. The student must pass the course before registering for
a dependent course unless an explicit curriculum transition rule states otherwise.
15. Curriculum Transition and Interpretation
15.1 This curriculum applies to students admitted from the 2026 cohort. Students from an earlier cohort continue under
their approved curriculum unless formally transferred to this version.
15.2 When a course is discontinued, the department may approve an equivalent replacement and publish the mapping.
Credits are counted once, using the approved category of the replacement course.
15.3 The Board of Studies may revise elective lists, course content and prerequisite mappings without changing the
degree requirements stated here. Any revision takes effect only after an official notice is issued.

Version: Version 1.0

Classification: Academic policy - approved for student reference
1. Purpose and Scope
1.1 These rules govern prerequisite and corequisite checks for undergraduate course registration at Northbridge
Institute of Technology. They apply together with the approved curriculum and the undergraduate academic regulations.
1.2 The rules are intended to ensure that students possess the knowledge required for a course while providing a clear
process for equivalence decisions, curriculum transitions and registration corrections.
2. Definitions
2.1 A prerequisite is a course or requirement that must be completed before registration in a dependent course.
2.2 A corequisite is a course that must have been completed earlier or must be registered in the same semester as the
related course.
2.3 Completion means earning a passing grade of P or higher. Attendance, audit status, an incomplete grade or prior
registration without a passing grade does not satisfy a prerequisite.
2.4 An equivalent course is a formally approved substitute that carries the same prerequisite effect as the course it
replaces.
3. General Registration Rules
3.1 The registration system checks prerequisites against the student's final academic record. A result awaiting
publication is not treated as a pass unless the Office of Examinations has issued an official provisional result.
3.2 A student may not remain registered in a dependent course after dropping its corequisite. The dependent course
must also be dropped unless the corequisite was completed in an earlier semester.
3.3 Meeting a prerequisite does not guarantee a seat. Registration remains subject to programme restrictions, timetable
compatibility, credit limits and course capacity.
3.4 The normal semester load is 18 to 24 credits. Approval is required above 24 credits, with an absolute limit of 27
credits. A student with a CGPA below 5.00 is ordinarily limited to 20 credits.
4. Computer Science Prerequisite Map

 CS202 Object-Oriented Programming - Prerequisite: CS101 Introduction to Programming.
 CS205 Web Technologies - Prerequisite: CS101 Introduction to Programming.

 MA201 Linear Algebra and Probability - Prerequisite: MA101 Engineering Mathematics I.

 CS302 Operating Systems - Prerequisites: CS201 Data Structures and CS203 Computer Organization.
 CS303 Computer Networks - Prerequisite: CS203 Computer Organization.
 CS304 Design and Analysis of Algorithms - Prerequisites: CS201 Data Structures and MA102 Engineering
 Mathematics II.
CS307 Systems Laboratory - Corequisites: CS302 Operating Systems and CS303 Computer Networks.

CS493 Project Phase II - Prerequisite: CS492 Project Phase I.
 6. Internship and Project Registration
6.1 CS491 Industry Internship requires prior departmental approval of the host organisation and proposed work. The
internship must have an approved duration of at least six weeks.
6.2 Registration for final-year project work normally requires at least 108 earned credits and no more than four active
backlogs. A department may also require specific supporting courses for the approved topic.
6.3 Project Phase II may not be registered until Project Phase I has been passed. A deferred or incomplete Phase I
result does not satisfy this requirement.
7. Failed, Repeated and Supplementary Courses
7.1 A failed prerequisite continues to block every dependent course until a passing result is recorded. Registration for a
supplementary examination does not by itself satisfy the prerequisite.
7.2 When a student repeats and passes a course, the updated result may be used for prerequisite checking from the
next registration correction window or from an earlier date announced by Academic Affairs.
7.3 If a prerequisite result changes after re-evaluation, the department shall review affected registrations. A student
remains responsible for reporting the changed result during the applicable correction period.
8. Transfer Credit and Equivalence
8.1 Transfer credit satisfies a prerequisite only when the Institute has approved an explicit course equivalence. Similar
course titles or equal credit values are not sufficient evidence.
8.2 The department evaluates the syllabus, learning outcomes, assessment level and contact hours before
recommending equivalence. The final decision is recorded by the Office of Academic Affairs.
8.3 An approved equivalence must identify the source course, the Northbridge course, the cohort to which it applies and
the date of approval.

9. Curriculum Transition
9.1 Students normally follow the curriculum assigned at admission. When a course is discontinued, the department
must publish a transition mapping before the relevant registration period.
9.2 A replacement course carries prerequisite effect only to the extent stated in the approved mapping. Credits may not
be counted twice when an earlier and replacement course cover the same requirement.
9.3 Students transferred to the 2026 curriculum must satisfy its prerequisite sequence unless the transition order
records an approved exception or equivalent course.
10. Exceptional Review
10.1 Prerequisites are not ordinarily waived. A student may request review only where an approved equivalence,
delayed official result, curriculum transition or administrative record error may not have been reflected in the registration
system.
10.2 A review request must include the course code, dependent course, relevant grade record and supporting approval.
The request should be submitted during registration or the published correction period.
10.3 Permission based only on personal assurance, informal faculty consent, work experience or self-study is not a
prerequisite waiver.
11. Registration Corrections
11.1 When a prerequisite error is discovered, the department may remove the dependent course before the add
deadline. After that deadline, Academic Affairs determines the academic notation and fee treatment under the
applicable regulations.
11.2 A student who knowingly supplies incorrect prerequisite information may be referred for disciplinary review.
Registration obtained through a system or record error does not create a right to continue in the course.
12. Interpretation
12.1 The approved programme curriculum is the primary source for course-specific prerequisite mappings. These rules
control the method by which those mappings are applied.
12.2 Where a later curriculum revision or official transition order conflicts with this document, the later and more specific
approved instruction prevails.

 NORTHBRIDGE INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY

 SEMESTER EXAMINATION REGULATIONS 2026
Document code: NIT/COE/SER/2026
Version: 1.0
Effective from: 1 August 2026
Classification: Academic policy - approved for student reference
1. Scope
1.1 These regulations govern end-semester, supplementary and other centrally administered examinations for
undergraduate programmes at Northbridge Institute of Technology.
1.2 Continuous assessment, laboratory evaluation, project review and other course-level assessments remain subject
to the approved course outline unless a provision of these regulations expressly applies.
1.3 The Controller of Examinations is responsible for examination schedules, registration, admit cards, secure conduct,
result processing and official examination records.
2. Examination eligibility
2.1 A student may appear in an end-semester examination only when registered for the course, academically eligible,
not subject to a relevant disciplinary restriction and compliant with the applicable attendance requirement.
2.2 The ordinary attendance requirement is at least 75 percent in the course. A student below that level must have
written approval under the Attendance Relaxation Guidelines before eligibility is confirmed.
2.3 Eligibility for one course does not establish eligibility for another. The final eligible-candidate list shall be prepared
course by course.
2.4 A student who has withdrawn from a course or whose registration was cancelled shall not appear in its examination.
3. Examination registration
3.1 Students shall submit the examination registration form within the period announced by the Controller of
Examinations. Registration shall include every eligible regular and repeat course intended for examination.
3.2 The examination registration deadline for the Autumn 2026 semester is 12 October 2026 unless changed by a later
numbered notice.
3.3 Late registration may be accepted for five working days after the ordinary deadline upon payment of the prescribed
late fee. No registration shall be accepted after release of the final timetable except to correct an established
institutional error.
3.4 A student is responsible for checking course codes, examination type and personal details before final submission.
4. Examination fees
4.1 The ordinary examination fee for regular courses is included in the semester academic fee unless a separate fee
schedule provides otherwise.
4.2 Repeat, supplementary and late applications may carry the fees published for the relevant academic year. Payment
does not by itself establish eligibility.
4.3 A failed payment transaction must be reported before the registration deadline with the transaction reference.
Duplicate verified payments shall be refunded through the Institute finance process.
5. Timetable
5.1 The provisional timetable shall normally be published at least four weeks before the first examination. Students may
report a direct timetable conflict within three working days.
5.2 The final timetable shall state the date, start time, duration and reporting instructions. Room allocation may be
published separately.
5.3 The Institute may revise the timetable for an emergency or administrative necessity. A revised numbered notice
supersedes the corresponding entry in the earlier timetable.

6. Admit cards
6.1 An admit card shall be issued after examination registration and eligibility verification. It may be withheld while an
attendance, fee, identity or disciplinary hold remains unresolved.
6.2 The student must check the admit card and report an incorrect course code or personal detail to the Examination
Office at least three working days before the relevant examination.
6.3 The admit card and Institute identity card must be produced at the examination venue. A temporary identity
authorization may be issued under the procedure announced by Student Services.
7. Reporting and entry
7.1 Students should report at least thirty minutes before the scheduled start. Entry after thirty minutes from the start time
shall not be permitted except under a written emergency direction from the Centre Superintendent.
7.2 A student shall not leave the examination room during the first thirty minutes or the final fifteen minutes of the
examination.
7.3 Additional writing time or another approved accommodation shall be provided only when authorized before the
examination under the Institute accessibility procedure.
8. Permitted and prohibited materials
8.1 Students may carry writing instruments and any material expressly permitted on the question paper or admit card.
8.2 Mobile phones, smart watches, communication devices, unauthorized notes and programmable storage devices are
prohibited inside the examination room unless deposited as directed.
8.3 A calculator may be used only when its permitted category is stated for the course. Sharing calculators or other
materials during the examination is not allowed.
9. Conduct during examination
9.1 Students shall follow seating instructions, maintain silence and comply with directions given by invigilators and the
Centre Superintendent.
9.2 The answer booklet must contain the required registration and course details but shall not contain a name, message
or identifying mark where anonymous evaluation is used.
9.3 No answer booklet or supplied examination material may be removed from the venue. Rough work must be
completed in the space or booklet provided.
9.4 Suspected possession or use of unauthorized material shall be recorded and handled under the Unfair Means
Regulations. The student shall be allowed to provide a written statement.
10. Absence and interrupted examinations
10.1 Absence from an examination ordinarily results in the recorded status Absent. A medical certificate does not
convert an absence into an examination attempt or passing result.
10.2 A student unable to complete an examination because of a documented medical emergency may apply for the next
permitted supplementary examination, subject to its eligibility rules.
10.3 If an examination is interrupted for all candidates due to an emergency, the Controller of Examinations may
resume, reschedule or cancel it and shall issue a written notice.
10.4 A question-paper error affecting assessment shall be reviewed by the Board of Examiners. Any approved
academic adjustment shall be applied consistently to all affected candidates.
11. Answer scripts
11.1 Answer scripts shall be collected, counted and transferred through the secure examination process. A student
must confirm that every supplementary booklet is attached before leaving.
11.2 Scripts and evaluation records shall be retained for the period prescribed by the examination-record schedule and
may be accessed only through an authorized review process.

12. Evaluation and moderation
12.1 Evaluation shall follow the approved marking scheme and course learning outcomes. Examiners shall report a
material ambiguity or error discovered during evaluation.
12.2 The Institute may use moderation, second evaluation or statistical review where required by the approved
assessment procedure.
12.3 Marks shall remain confidential until results are formally approved and published. Informal communication by an
examiner does not constitute an official result.
13. Result publication
13.1 Semester results shall be published through the official student information system after approval by the competent
academic authority.
13.2 A result may be temporarily withheld for an unresolved examination irregularity, eligibility issue, missing
assessment component or administrative verification.
13.3 A student should report an apparent result-processing error within five working days of publication. Correction of a
processing error is distinct from re-evaluation of academic judgment.
14. Re-evaluation and script access
14.1 A student may request re-evaluation only for courses and assessment components permitted under the
Re-evaluation Policy 2026.
14.2 The application must be submitted within seven calendar days of result publication and may cover no more than
three courses in a semester.
14.3 Payment of the prescribed fee and submission of the correct application do not guarantee a change of grade. The
revised result, if any, shall replace the earlier result.
15. Supplementary examination
15.1 A supplementary examination may be offered for eligible failed or absent courses according to the Supplementary
Examination Guidelines 2026.
15.2 Registration for a supplementary examination is separate from ordinary semester registration. The student must
satisfy the announced deadline, fee and course eligibility conditions.
15.3 A supplementary examination does not remove the original attempt from the academic record.
16. Special arrangements and emergencies
16.1 The Controller of Examinations may arrange an alternate venue, additional invigilation or another reasonable
measure for an approved accessibility, security or emergency requirement.
16.2 Requests for ordinary scheduling convenience, travel plans or private employment shall not be grounds for a
special examination.
16.3 Where a public emergency affects a group of students, the Institute shall issue a common decision rather than
require repetitive individual requests where practicable.
17. Appeals and records
17.1 An appeal concerning application of these regulations must be submitted to the Controller of Examinations within
five working days of the disputed decision.
17.2 Academic judgment in the award of marks may be challenged only through the authorized re-evaluation process.
18. Commencement
18.1 These regulations take effect on 1 August 2026 and apply to examinations connected with courses beginning on or
after that date.
18.2 A later numbered circular may amend a deadline or operational instruction. The later effective notice shall prevail
for the matter it expressly changes.

1. Purpose
1.1 These guidelines describe the procedure for registering for centrally administered undergraduate examinations at
Northbridge Institute of Technology.
1.2 They apply to regular, repeat and supplementary examination registrations unless a later examination notice states
a different procedure for a specified examination period.
1.3 Registration records the student's intention to appear. It does not override course registration, attendance
requirements, disciplinary restrictions or another condition of examination eligibility.
2. Registration period
2.1 Registration for the Autumn 2026 end-semester examinations opens on 28 September 2026 and closes at 5:00 p.m.
on 12 October 2026.
2.2 A later numbered notice issued by the Controller of Examinations may extend or revise the dates. An effective
extension notice shall prevail over the dates stated in these guidelines.
2.3 Students should not wait for the final day to register. A technical problem affecting only an individual device or
internet connection does not automatically extend the deadline.
3. Students required to register
3.1 Every student intending to appear in a regular end-semester examination must complete examination registration,
even when the examination fee is included in the semester fee.
3.2 A student repeating a failed course must include that course in the examination registration after confirming valid
course or repeat registration with the department.
3.3 A student appearing only in a supplementary examination must follow the separate supplementary registration
window announced for that examination.
4. Courses available for registration
4.1 The registration system displays courses based on the student's approved semester registration and eligible
repeat-course record.
4.2 A missing course must be reported before the deadline. Students shall not select an unrelated course code as a
temporary substitute.
4.3 A withdrawn, cancelled or unregistered course shall not be added to the examination registration unless Academic
Affairs has corrected the underlying academic record.
5. Registration steps
 a. Sign in through the official student information system and open the Examination Registration section.
 b. Verify the programme, semester, name and student registration number.
 c. Select each eligible regular, repeat or approved backlog course intended for examination.
 d. Confirm the examination type and review any displayed attendance or administrative hold.
 e. Pay any applicable fee and submit the form before the stated deadline.
 f. Download or retain the acknowledgement containing the submission number and timestamp.
 6. Student verification
6.1 Before submission, the student must confirm that every selected course code and title matches the academic
record.

7. Fees and payment
7.1 No separate examination fee is charged for ordinary regular courses when that fee is included in the semester
academic fee.
7.2 Repeat, supplementary and late registrations are subject to the fee schedule published for the 2026-27 academic
year.
7.3 A payment is complete only when the registration system records a successful transaction. A bank debit without
system confirmation must be reported with the transaction reference.
7.4 A verified duplicate payment shall be forwarded for refund. Refund processing does not delay a valid registration
already confirmed by the system.
8. Late registration
8.1 Late registration is available for five working days after the ordinary deadline and requires payment of the prescribed
late fee.
8.2 After the late period, registration may be accepted only to correct an established institutional error and only before
release of the final examination timetable.
8.3 Personal oversight, travel, failure to check notices or an unreported payment problem is not normally an institutional
error.
9. Correction period
9.1 A student may request correction of a submitted registration within three working days of submission or by the close
of the ordinary registration period, whichever is later.
9.2 The request must identify the submission number, affected course and correction required. The Examination Office
may seek confirmation from the department.
9.3 Correction of an examination registration cannot be used to create academic course registration after the academic
add and drop period.
10. Attendance and eligibility holds
10.1 A course may appear in the registration form while attendance verification remains pending. Final eligibility will be
determined under the Undergraduate Attendance Policy 2026.
10.2 A student below 75 percent attendance must obtain an approved relaxation decision, where eligible, before the
examination eligibility list is finalized.
10.3 Submission of Form ATT-07 does not by itself remove an attendance hold.
11. Other holds
11.1 The system may display a hold relating to identity verification, disciplinary restriction, unresolved academic
registration or another officially recorded requirement.
11.2 The student must contact the office identified in the hold message. The Examination Office shall not remove a hold
owned by another authorized office without written clearance.
12. Repeat and backlog courses
12.1 A repeat course must be registered using the current valid course code or an approved equivalent identified by the
department.
12.2 Where a curriculum revision has replaced a course, the department must map the earlier course to the approved
examination or repeat arrangement before registration.
12.3 A student shall not register for two examinations scheduled at the same time without first reporting the conflict and
receiving an approved resolution.
13. Registration acknowledgement
13.1 The acknowledgement is evidence of submission but is not an admit card and does not guarantee final eligibility.
13.2 Students should retain the acknowledgement until results for the examination period have been published.

15.1 A widespread system interruption confirmed by the Institute may result in an extension announced through a
numbered notice.
15.2 For an individual technical incident, the student should capture the error message and report it to the service desk

15.3 Screenshots without a timestamp, student identifier or matching service record may be insufficient to establish that

16.1 Cancellation of examination registration does not cancel academic course registration. A course withdrawal must
follow the academic regulations.
16.2 A student who decides not to appear after registration will ordinarily be recorded Absent unless the course is

16.3 Fees paid for a repeat or supplementary registration are not refundable solely because the student chooses not to
appear.
17. Special cases
17.1 A student on an approved exchange, accessibility arrangement or other formally approved academic plan should
contact the Examination Office during the ordinary registration period.
17.2 Requests for a special examination based only on personal travel, employment or scheduling convenience shall
not be processed through registration correction.
17.3 An institutional emergency affecting a group of students shall be handled through a common notice where
practicable.
18. Records and responsibility
18.1 The Institute shall retain the submitted registration, transaction status, correction history and final
examination-course list as part of the examination record.
18.2 Students remain responsible for reviewing official notices, meeting deadlines and preserving their
acknowledgement.

working days of the communicated decision.

general request to overlook the deadline is not sufficient.

 NORTHBRIDGE INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY
 Office of the Controller of Examinations
 RE-EVALUATION POLICY 2026
Document code: NIT/COE/REV/2026
Version: 1.0
Effective from: 1 August 2026
Classification: Academic policy - approved for student reference
1. Purpose
1.1 This policy provides a formal process for requesting fresh academic evaluation of an eligible written end-semester
examination answer script.
1.2 Re-evaluation is intended to check whether the submitted answers have been assessed appropriately under the
approved marking scheme. It is not a general appeal against course design, question-paper difficulty or academic
standards.
1.3 Correction of an omitted mark, totaling error or result-processing error may be completed administratively and does
not require academic re-evaluation when no judgment of answer quality is involved.
2. Assessments eligible for re-evaluation
2.1 A written end-semester examination evaluated through an answer script is eligible unless the course has been
expressly excluded by an approved academic rule.
2.2 A student may apply for no more than three courses from the same semester examination result.
2.3 Eligibility does not depend on whether the original grade is passing or failing.
3. Assessments not eligible
 a. Laboratory, studio, workshop, clinical, field or performance assessments.
 b. Projects, dissertations, seminars, presentations, vivas or internship evaluations.
 c. Continuous-assessment components such as quizzes, assignments and mid-semester examinations unless a
 separate rule applies.
d. Answer scripts already subject to a court, disciplinary or unfair-means process that prevents ordinary result review.
 4. Application deadline
4.1 The application must be submitted within seven calendar days of official publication of the relevant semester result.
4.2 The publication date shown in the student information system is used to calculate the deadline. The day after
publication is counted as day one.
4.3 A delayed application may be accepted only when a documented Institute system failure or another circumstance
recognized by the Controller of Examinations prevented timely submission.
5. Application procedure
 a. Open the Re-evaluation section in the official student information system.
 b. Select no more than three eligible courses from the published result.
 c. Confirm the course code, original grade and examination period.
 d. Pay the prescribed fee for each selected course.
 e. Submit the application and retain the acknowledgement number.
 6. Fee
6.1 The applicable fee shall be the amount stated in the examination fee schedule for 2026-27.
6.2 A payment without a submitted application does not create a re-evaluation request. Failed or duplicate transactions
must be reported using the payment reference.
6.3 The fee is refundable only when the Institute cannot process the application because the assessment is ineligible or
the answer script is unavailable for a reason not attributable to the student.

7. Preliminary scrutiny
7.1 The Examination Office shall verify the deadline, course eligibility, application count, payment status and availability
of the answer script.
7.2 An incomplete or ineligible application shall be rejected with a brief reason. A correctable system-record error may
be resolved before rejection.
7.3 Acceptance for processing does not indicate that the original evaluation was incorrect.
8. Selection of re-evaluator
8.1 The answer script shall be assigned to a qualified examiner who did not perform the original evaluation, where
reasonably practicable.
8.2 The identity of the student and the original examiner shall not be disclosed to the re-evaluator when anonymous
processing is available.
8.3 The re-evaluator shall use the approved question paper, marking scheme and academic instructions applicable to
the original examination.
9. Scope of re-evaluation
9.1 The re-evaluator shall assess every attempted answer and verify that marks have been awarded according to the
approved scheme.
9.2 The re-evaluator may correct an award that is unsupported, an answer that was overlooked or a totaling issue
discovered during review.
9.3 The student's answers shall not be improved, completed or interpreted using material not present in the submitted
script.
10. Difference in marks
10.1 The re-evaluated marks shall replace the original marks when the resulting grade differs from the original grade.
10.2 When the difference is unusually large under the moderation threshold approved by the Examination Board, the
script may be referred for an additional review before the result is finalized.
10.3 The finalized re-evaluation result may increase, decrease or leave unchanged the original marks and grade.
11. Processing time
11.1 The Institute will ordinarily publish the re-evaluation outcome within twenty working days after the application
window closes.
11.2 A delay may occur when an examiner is unavailable, a moderation review is required or the answer script must be
reconstructed from secure records.
11.3 The Examination Office shall issue a notice when a material delay affects a group of applications.
12. Publication of outcome
12.1 The outcome shall be published through the official student information system and shall show whether the result
is changed or unchanged.
12.2 When a grade changes, the revised grade shall replace the earlier grade in the semester result and CGPA
calculation.
12.3 The complete academic record may continue to show that the result was revised through the authorized process.
13. Effect on progression and registration
13.1 A student should continue with applicable registration and progression requirements while re-evaluation is pending
unless Academic Affairs gives a written interim direction.
13.2 A later improved grade shall be applied to eligibility and progression decisions that have not become final, subject
to programme rules.
13.3 The Institute is not responsible for a missed external opportunity based on an unchanged result while a
re-evaluation application is pending.

14. Answer-script access
14.1 Where answer-script viewing is offered, it is a separate service from re-evaluation and must be requested through
the procedure announced by the Examination Office.
14.2 Viewing allows the student to inspect the processed script but does not permit alteration, annotation, photography
or removal of the script.
14.3 Failure to request viewing does not affect eligibility to apply for re-evaluation within the deadline.
15. Administrative error correction
15.1 A student who identifies an apparent omitted component, incorrect totaling or result-entry error should report it
within five working days of result publication.
15.2 The Examination Office may correct a verified administrative error without charging a re-evaluation fee.
15.3 When review of the alleged error requires fresh academic judgment, the matter shall proceed only through an
eligible and timely re-evaluation application.
16. Confidentiality and integrity
16.1 Examiner identities, internal moderation records and secure answer-script handling details shall remain
confidential except where disclosure is legally required.
16.2 A student or another person shall not contact an evaluator to influence or inquire about a pending re-evaluation.
16.3 Fabricated payment evidence, altered result records or attempted interference may be referred for disciplinary
action.
17. Review of procedural error
17.1 The academic judgment of the re-evaluator is final and is not subject to repeated re-evaluation.
17.2 A student may request review by the Controller of Examinations within three working days when the complaint
concerns a procedural error, wrong script, incomplete processing or incorrect publication of the finalized result.
17.3 A procedural review shall not become a third academic evaluation unless the Examination Board determines that
the authorized process was not completed.
18. Records
18.1 The Institute shall retain the application, payment status, evaluation record and result change according to the
examination-record retention schedule.
18.2 Anonymized re-evaluation statistics may be used for assessment review, examiner development and quality
assurance.
19. Commencement
19.1 This policy takes effect on 1 August 2026 and applies to results published for courses beginning on or after that
date.
19.2 It shall be read with the Semester Examination Regulations 2026 and any later numbered notification expressly
amending the re-evaluation process.

Version: 1.0

Classification: Academic policy - approved for student reference
1. Purpose
1.1 These guidelines regulate supplementary undergraduate examinations conducted by Northbridge Institute of
Technology for eligible failed or absent courses.
1.2 A supplementary examination provides an additional assessment opportunity but does not replace ordinary course
participation, academic registration or the requirements of the original course.
1.3 The Controller of Examinations shall announce the courses, registration period, fees, timetable and result date for
each supplementary cycle.
2. Courses covered
2.1 A written theory course with an end-semester examination may be included when the department confirms that a
valid question paper and examiner are available.
2.2 A laboratory, studio, project, seminar, internship, field or continuous-assessment component is not ordinarily offered
through a supplementary written examination.
2.3 When a course includes both theory and practical components, the department shall specify which component must
be repeated and whether the earlier passing component remains valid.
3. Student eligibility
3.1 A student who received grade F in an eligible course may register for the next announced supplementary
examination for that course.
3.2 A student recorded Absent in the ordinary examination may register when the underlying course registration and
attendance eligibility were valid.
3.3 A student whose ordinary examination eligibility was denied for attendance shortage may not use the
supplementary examination to bypass that decision and must repeat the course unless a specific academic order
provides otherwise.
3.4 A student subject to an unresolved unfair-means proceeding or relevant disciplinary restriction is not eligible until the
authorized decision permits registration.
4. Number of courses
4.1 A student may register for no more than four supplementary courses in one examination cycle.
4.2 The timetable may limit the practical number of courses that can be attempted. The Institute is not required to
arrange a special sitting for conflicts created by selecting multiple supplementary courses.
5. Registration
5.1 Supplementary registration is separate from ordinary semester examination registration and must be completed
during the announced window.
5.2 The student shall select the correct course code, examination cycle and attempt type, pay the applicable fee and
retain the acknowledgement.
5.3 A submitted registration remains subject to verification of course history, eligibility and any academic hold.
6. Registration period for the first cycle
6.1 For the first supplementary cycle following the Autumn 2026 results, registration opens on 11 January 2027 and
closes at 5:00 p.m. on 18 January 2027.
6.2 Late registration may be accepted for three working days after the deadline with the prescribed late fee.
6.3 A later numbered notice may revise these dates. The later effective notice shall prevail.
