7. Fees and acknowledgement
7.1 A separate fee is payable for each supplementary course according to the examination fee schedule for 2026-27.
7.2 A debit without a successful registration acknowledgement must be reported before the deadline with the payment
transaction reference.
7.3 A verified duplicate payment shall be processed for refund. A fee is not refundable solely because the student
chooses not to appear.
8. Timetable
8.1 The timetable shall normally be published at least ten calendar days before the first supplementary examination.
8.2 The first cycle is expected to be conducted from 1 February 2027 to 6 February 2027, subject to the final timetable.
8.3 A later timetable or emergency notice may revise the date, time or venue. Students are responsible for checking the
final notice.
9. Admit cards
9.1 Admit cards shall be issued after registration and eligibility verification. The student must check the course code and
personal details.
9.2 The supplementary registration acknowledgement is not an admit card and does not authorize entry to the
examination venue.
9.3 An admit-card error should be reported at least two working days before the affected examination.
10. Conduct of examination
10.1 The reporting, identity, permitted-material and examination-conduct provisions of the Semester Examination
Regulations 2026 apply to supplementary examinations.
10.2 The supplementary paper shall assess the same approved course outcomes as the ordinary end-semester
examination, although the questions may differ.
10.3 No special paper shall be arranged for a student who misses the supplementary examination, except under an
Institute-wide emergency decision.
11. Evaluation and grading
11.1 The supplementary examination shall be evaluated under the approved marking scheme and passing standard for
the course.
11.2 Where the course grade includes retained continuous-assessment marks, the department shall apply the approved
course rule. Continuous-assessment marks shall not be altered merely because a supplementary examination is taken.
11.3 The grade obtained after the supplementary examination shall be recorded under the Institute grade-replacement
and transcript rules.
12. Result publication
12.1 Supplementary results shall ordinarily be published within fifteen working days after the final examination in the
cycle.
12.2 A result may be withheld for an unresolved irregularity, missing academic record or evaluation verification.
12.3 A student should report an apparent processing error within five working days of result publication.
13. Re-evaluation
13.1 An eligible supplementary written examination may be submitted for re-evaluation under the Re-evaluation Policy
2026.
13.2 The application must be made within seven calendar days of supplementary result publication and counts toward
the applicable course limit for that result cycle.

14. Academic effect

original attempt from the academic record.

2026.
14.3 A result published after a registration or progression deadline shall be applied to decisions that remain open. It
does not automatically reverse a completed external selection process.

15.1 When a course code has changed, the department shall identify the approved equivalent or transition examination.
15.2 A discontinued course may be offered for a limited number of supplementary cycles or replaced with an approved
course requirement.

independently.

16.1 A student absent from a supplementary examination shall be recorded Absent. The examination fee will not
ordinarily be carried forward.

16.3 Where an emergency affects the conduct of an examination for a group of candidates, the Controller of
Examinations may reschedule it through a numbered notice.

final result as part of the examination record.

1. Purpose and Application
1.1 This policy governs refunds arising from undergraduate admission cancellation, programme withdrawal, Institute
cancellation, duplicate payment and refundable deposits during the 2026-27 academic year.
1.2 The policy applies together with the Tuition Fee Structure 2026. Hostel, mess and transport refunds are governed by

1.3 Dropping an individual course from a normal full-time semester does not ordinarily create a tuition refund because
tuition is charged as a semester package. A separately charged repeat or Summer course may qualify only where this
policy expressly permits a refund.
2. Definitions
2.1 Classes begin on the teaching start date stated for the relevant semester in the official academic calendar.
2.2 The withdrawal date is the date on which the Registrar's Office acknowledges a complete formal withdrawal request.
The date on which a student stops attending classes is not the withdrawal date.
2.3 Tuition means the recurring tuition fee of INR 75,000 per semester. It does not include academic services,
laboratory and technology, student activity or examination administration charges.
3. Withdrawal-Based Tuition Refund
 Before classes begin - 80 percent of tuition, equal to INR 60,000 for the standard semester tuition.
 Days 1-7 after classes begin - 60 percent of tuition, equal to INR 45,000.
 Days 8-14 after classes begin - 40 percent of tuition, equal to INR 30,000.
 Days 15-30 after classes begin - 20 percent of tuition, equal to INR 15,000.
 After day 30 - No withdrawal-based tuition refund is available, except where another provision of this policy applies.
 3.1 The day on which classes begin is day 1. Calendar days, including weekends and Institute holidays, are counted

non-tuition charges are refunded in full.

# Hostel Rules FAQ

This FAQ summarises the main residential rules for students living in Northbridge Institute of Technology hostels. Residents remain responsible for the complete residential agreement, safety instructions and official notices issued during the semester.

## Who may live in an Institute hostel?

Only a student with a current hostel allotment may occupy the assigned room. The allotment applies to the named student, room and semester. It cannot be transferred, exchanged or sublet without written approval from the Student Housing Office.

Visitors, friends and students on the waiting list must not stay overnight in a hostel room.

## What must I present at check-in?

A student must present the final allotment notice, Institute ID or admission letter, hostel payment acknowledgement and one recent passport-size photograph. The student must also complete the room inventory and provide current guardian and emergency-contact details.

Any existing damage or missing item should be recorded on the inventory before the room is accepted.

## When are hostel and mess payments due?

The Autumn 2026 hostel allocation circular states that a student offered a room must complete payment by 5:00 p.m. on 1 August 2026. A later offer made from the waiting list will carry its own payment deadline.

The notified semester charges are INR 28,000 for the hostel room and INR 24,000 as the mess advance. A hostel caution deposit of INR 5,000 is payable at first allotment. The applicable fee structure and residential agreement govern collection, adjustment and refund.

## Can I choose or change my room?

Students may state a room preference during application, but a preference is not guaranteed. Allocation depends on eligibility, room category, approved accommodation needs and available capacity.

A room change requires written approval. Students must not exchange keys, move belongings into another room or occupy a vacant bed while a request is pending.

## Can another person use my room?

No. A room or bed may be used only by the student to whom it is allotted. Lending a room key or access credential, allowing unauthorised overnight occupancy, or collecting payment for room access is prohibited.

## What are the visitor rules?

Visitors may meet residents only in designated common areas during notified visiting hours. The resident is responsible for the visitor's conduct and must follow the entry-register and identification procedure.

The Warden may restrict visitors during examinations, emergencies, maintenance work or another period requiring additional security. Overnight visitors are not permitted unless the Student Housing Office has issued specific written approval for an official purpose.

## Are there hostel entry timings?

Residents must follow the entry and quiet-hour timings displayed by the hostel. A student expecting to return after the notified entry time should use the late-entry procedure and provide the required reason and contact information.

Repeated unexplained late entry, false entries or bypassing access controls may be referred to the Warden. Entry restrictions do not prevent emergency access or approved academic, medical or placement-related movement.

## What are the quiet hours?

Quiet hours normally apply from 10:30 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. Residents must keep conversations, calls, music and electronic devices at a level that cannot be heard outside their room during this period.

Noise that disrupts study, sleep or official activity is not acceptable at any time. Common rooms may carry separate hours displayed at the entrance.

## May I cook in my room?

Cooking in student rooms is prohibited. Heating coils, hot plates, gas appliances and other exposed heating devices must not be kept or used in a room.

Only electrical items expressly permitted by the hostel may be used. Approved kettles or similar low-power appliances, where allowed, must be operated safely and disconnected after use. The Warden may remove an unsafe or prohibited appliance.

## Are smoking and alcohol permitted?

Smoking, vaping, alcohol, illegal drugs and possession of related prohibited material are not permitted in hostel buildings or other areas covered by Institute policy. A suspected medical emergency should be reported immediately rather than concealed because of possible disciplinary action.

## How should rooms and common areas be maintained?

Residents must keep their rooms reasonably clean and use waste-disposal points correctly. Corridors, stairways, exits and fire equipment must remain unobstructed.

Furniture must not be removed, dismantled or transferred between rooms. Nails, permanent adhesive, paint or another alteration that damages Institute property may lead to restoration charges.

## When may staff enter a room?

Authorised staff may enter for scheduled inspection, maintenance, safety checks, welfare concerns or an emergency. Advance notice will normally be given for routine work. Immediate access may be required when there is a fire alarm, water leak, electrical hazard, medical concern or reasonable belief of a serious rule violation.

## What should I do if something needs repair?

Submit a maintenance request through the hostel service portal and include the room number, problem and urgency. Water leaks, exposed wiring, smoke, a damaged lock or another immediate hazard must also be reported to the duty supervisor without delay.

Students must not arrange structural, electrical or plumbing repairs independently.

## Who is responsible for loss or damage?

Residents are responsible for reasonable care of their rooms, keys and issued property. The cost of damage beyond ordinary wear may be charged to the responsible student. Shared-area damage may be investigated before responsibility is assigned.

Students should secure money, documents and electronic devices. The Institute does not accept responsibility for unattended personal property except where liability is established under applicable law.

## What if I lose my room key or access card?

Report the loss immediately to the hostel office or duty supervisor. A temporary access arrangement may be made after identity is verified. Replacement and lock-change charges may apply.

A lost student ID card must also be reported through Student ID Card Services so its electronic access can be blocked.

## Can I remain in the hostel during a vacation?

Hostel accommodation does not automatically continue through a vacation or semester break. Students requiring approved vacation residence must apply by the announced deadline and provide the academic, internship, travel or other supporting reason requested by the Student Housing Office.

Some buildings may close or operate with reduced services during a break, and residents may be moved to designated rooms.

## How do I withdraw from hostel accommodation?

A resident must submit the prescribed cancellation request, clear room inventory and key obligations, and complete the check-out procedure. Simply leaving the room or handing a key to another student does not close the hostel account.

Any refund or deduction is determined under the applicable fee policy and residential agreement. The check-out record should be retained until the student's account is updated.

## What happens if hostel rules are broken?

The Warden may issue an advisory, require corrective action or refer the matter for disciplinary review, depending on its seriousness and frequency. Serious safety, violence, harassment, unauthorised occupancy, substance or property-related matters may lead to immediate protective measures while they are investigated.

A student will ordinarily be informed of the allegation and given an opportunity to respond under the applicable Institute procedure.

## How do I report an emergency or safety concern?

For an immediate threat to life or property, contact campus security at extension 2000 and alert the duty supervisor. Fire alarms must be treated as genuine, and residents must use the marked evacuation route without waiting to collect belongings.

Non-emergency residential concerns may be reported to `housing.office@northbridge.example`. Reports should identify the hostel, room or location and provide enough information for follow-up.

## Document authority

The Director of Student Housing maintains this FAQ. The residential agreement, Institute regulations and later dated official notices take precedence if they impose a more specific or updated requirement.

# Library Services FAQ

This document explains the main services and rules of the Northbridge Institute of Technology Central Library. It applies from 1 August 2026 unless a later official notice changes a particular service.

## When is the library open?

During teaching weeks, the library is open from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m., Monday to Friday, and from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on Saturday. It is closed on Sundays and Institute holidays. Extended examination hours, when approved, are announced separately through official channels.

## Who can use the library?

Library membership is activated for registered students and current employees. A valid Institute ID card is required to enter controlled areas, borrow material and collect reserved items. Access may be suspended when a person's Institute registration or employment is inactive.

## How many books may a student borrow?

An undergraduate student may borrow up to five circulating books at a time. The standard loan period is 14 calendar days. A book may be renewed twice if it is not overdue, another user has not placed a hold on it and the item is not part of a restricted collection.

## How do holds and reservations work?

A student may place a hold on a circulating book through the library catalogue. When the book becomes available, the library sends a notice to the student's Institute email address. The item is held at the service desk for two working days and is then offered to the next person in the queue.

## What happens when a book is overdue?

The overdue charge is INR 5 per book per day for the first 14 overdue days and INR 10 per book per day after that. Borrowing privileges are suspended while an item remains overdue. A reminder is a courtesy; not receiving one does not cancel the return date or the charge.

## What should I do if a book is lost or damaged?

Report the loss or damage to the service desk promptly. The library may require an approved replacement copy of the same edition or payment of the assessed replacement cost, together with an INR 100 processing charge. Writing, highlighting, water damage, missing pages and damage to labels or security tags may be treated as damage. The library will confirm the settlement amount in writing.

## Can reference and course-reserve material be borrowed?

Reference works, archival material, theses and items marked "Library Use Only" must normally remain in the library. A course-reserve item may have a shorter loan period or overnight use when that permission is shown in the catalogue. The due time printed on the loan record applies.

## How can I use journals, databases and e-books?

Current students and employees may use licensed digital resources with their Institute credentials. Off-campus access is available through the library's remote-access portal where the licence permits it. Credentials must not be shared, and systematic downloading or redistribution of licensed content is prohibited.

## Are printing and scanning available?

Self-service printing and scanning are available during library hours. Current charges are displayed at the service desk and in the print portal. Users are responsible for complying with copyright and licence conditions when copying any material.

## Can study rooms be reserved?

Group-study rooms may be booked through the library portal by registered students. A booking may be released if the group does not arrive within 15 minutes. Quiet-study areas are not reservable and must be used without group discussion or calls.

## Does the library provide interlibrary loans?

Material not held by the Central Library may be requested through the interlibrary-loan service. A student may have up to three active requests. Lending-library restrictions apply, and any external copying, postage or replacement charge is passed to the requester after notice.

## What accessibility support is available?

The library provides step-free access, adjustable study spaces and assistance in locating or collecting material. Students who need an alternative format or another approved accommodation should contact the service desk or the Institute accessibility office as early as possible.

## What conduct is expected inside the library?

Users must follow the noise designation of each area. Food is not permitted near collections or computers; covered drinking water is allowed in designated areas. Personal belongings must not be used to reserve unattended seats. The Institute is not responsible for items left behind.

## What if my student ID card is lost?

Report the card through Student ID Card Services and inform the library. Borrowing on the missing card will be blocked. Temporary borrowing permission may be issued after identity and current registration are verified; a photograph or photocopy of the missing card is not accepted as a substitute.

## How do I obtain library clearance?

Students completing, withdrawing from or transferring out of a programme must return all borrowed material and settle confirmed charges. Clearance is recorded after the library account has been checked. Returning books to a department or another student does not complete library clearance.

## How can I contact the library?

Email `library.help@northbridge.example`, call extension 2204 or visit the Central Library service desk during opening hours. Include your student number and any catalogue, loan or request reference when asking about a specific transaction.

## Document authority

The Director of Library Services maintains this FAQ. If it conflicts with a later dated Institute regulation or official circular, the later authoritative document applies. Service-hour changes and temporary closures may be announced separately without issuing a new version of this FAQ.

1. Purpose and Coverage
1.1 The Institute Merit Scholarship recognises sustained academic achievement among full-time undergraduate
students of Northbridge Institute of Technology.
1.2 Awards are made for one academic year and are subject to the eligibility, ranking, renewal and funding rules in this
policy. A scholarship is a fee concession and does not guarantee continued support in a later year.
2. Scholarship Categories
 Merit Scholarship A - A tuition concession of 50 percent, equal to INR 37,500 per semester under the 2026 fee
 structure. It is normally offered to students ranked within the top 3 percent of the eligible programme and year group.
Merit Scholarship B - A tuition concession of 25 percent, equal to INR 18,750 per semester. It is normally offered to
 the next 7 percent of the eligible programme and year group.
2.1 The number of awards is calculated separately for each programme and year group. A fraction of 0.5 or above is
rounded up, subject to at least five eligible students in the group.
2.2 The Scholarship Committee may leave an award unfilled when no applicant meets the minimum standard. Unused
awards are not automatically transferred between programmes.
3. Continuing-Student Eligibility
3.1 The applicant must be registered as a full-time undergraduate student and must have completed the preceding
academic year at the Institute.
3.2 A minimum cumulative grade point average of 8.00 is required. Ranking is based on the final CGPA recorded after
the regular result and any completed re-evaluation process.
3.3 The applicant must have passed every registered compulsory course from the preceding academic year and must
not have an F or unresolved I grade.
3.4 The applicant must have earned at least 36 credits during the preceding academic year unless a lower approved
curriculum load applied.
3.5 The applicant must have no active disciplinary action or finding of examination misconduct.
3.6 The applicant must not have been debarred from an examination for attendance shortage. An approved attendance
relaxation does not by itself disqualify the applicant.
4. Newly Admitted Students
4.1 A limited first-year award may be offered using the Institute's approved admission merit list. The admission notice
states the applicable rank range and number of awards.
4.2 A first-year award is provisional until the student completes registration, verifies admission documents and pays any
balance not covered by the scholarship.

# Student ID Card Services

The Institute identity card is the primary identification document for students of Northbridge Institute of Technology. This guide explains how cards are issued, activated, replaced and returned.

## First issue of a student ID card

New students receive an ID card after admission, identity verification and completion of the required registration steps. The Student Services Centre will announce the collection schedule for each programme.

Students must collect their cards personally and present the original admission acknowledgement or another government-issued photo identity document. A card will not be released to a friend, class representative or family member.

The first card issued during admission is included in the student registration process and does not carry a separate card fee.

## Information printed on the card

The card normally shows the student's name, photograph, student number, programme, card issue date and validity period. Electronic records connected to the card may also be used for library access, attendance systems, examinations and approved campus facilities.

A student should check the printed details at the time of collection. A printing error reported within five working days will be corrected without a replacement charge.

## Card activation

Most new cards are activated before collection. Access to individual services may take up to one working day after the card is issued. If the card is recognised by one service but rejected by another, the student should report the affected service and location to the Student Services Centre.

Activation does not override a restriction placed by the Library, Finance and Accounts, Student Housing, the Controller of Examinations or another authorised office.

## Lost or stolen cards

A lost or stolen card must be reported immediately through the student portal. Reporting the card blocks its electronic use and creates a service reference number. Students should also report theft to campus security when the circumstances require it.

The Institute is not responsible for unauthorised use that occurs before the loss is reported. A card reported as lost must not be used if it is later found. The student should return it to the Student Services Centre for disposal.

## Replacement of a lost card

After reporting the loss, the student may submit an ID card replacement request through the portal. The request must include the service reference number and a recent photograph if the existing photograph no longer meets identification requirements.

The replacement charge is INR 500. Payment must be made through the Institute payment portal after the request is accepted. A payment receipt without an approved request does not authorise card production.

Replacement cards are normally ready within five working days after approval and confirmed payment. This period may be longer during admission, examination or mass-renewal activity.

## Damaged or malfunctioning cards

A damaged or unreadable card should be presented at the Student Services Centre. If the card has failed under ordinary use and shows no avoidable physical damage, it may be replaced without charge after inspection.

A replacement charge may apply when the card is cracked, deliberately altered, punched, cut, exposed to excessive heat or otherwise damaged through misuse. The old card must be surrendered before the replacement is issued.

## Changes to personal or academic details

The Student Services Centre cannot change a name, date of birth, programme or other official record only on the basis of a card request. The underlying student record must first be corrected by the authorised academic or admissions office.

After the approved change appears in the student information system, a revised card may be requested. No replacement charge applies when the reissue is required solely because of an approved Institute record correction or an Institute-directed programme change.

## Temporary identification letter

A student waiting for a replacement card may request a temporary identification letter. It is issued only after identity and current registration are verified and is normally valid for seven calendar days.

The letter does not automatically provide electronic door access, library borrowing or examination entry. The office responsible for each service decides whether additional verification is required. Examination identification remains subject to instructions issued by the Controller of Examinations.

## Proper use of the card

The student ID card is personal and must not be lent, copied, altered or used by another person. Students must present it when requested by an authorised Institute employee or security officer acting in an official capacity.

Possession of another student's card, use of an altered card or assistance in unauthorised access may result in withdrawal of the card and action under Institute regulations.

## Expiry and renewal

The validity date is printed on the card. Continuing students will receive renewal instructions when a physical replacement or electronic extension is required. A student must not modify an expiry date or continue using an expired card as proof of current registration.

## Graduation, withdrawal or termination of registration

The card remains Institute property. It must be returned when requested after graduation, withdrawal, cancellation of admission or termination of registration. Returning the card does not by itself complete academic, financial, library or hostel clearance.

## Contact and service hours

The Student Services Centre is open from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday to Friday, except Institute holidays. Students may email `student.services@northbridge.example` or call extension 2102.

Requests concerning a specific card should include the student number and portal service reference. Full identity-document numbers should not be sent by ordinary email.

## Document authority

The Registrar maintains this service guide. A later dated Institute regulation, examination instruction or official notice takes precedence where it addresses the same matter.

CAMPUS EMERGENCY CONTACTS AND INITIAL RESPONSE

Document ID: NIT-SAF-EMR-2026
Maintained by: Campus Safety Office
Published: 24 July 2026
Effective from: 1 August 2026
Version: 1.0

USE OF THIS DOCUMENT

This document provides the first contact and immediate action for common campus emergencies. It does not replace instructions from emergency services, Campus Security, medical personnel, fire wardens or other authorised responders.

When calling, state your name, exact location, the nature of the emergency, the number of people affected and a telephone number on which you can be reached. Do not end the call until the responder confirms that the required information has been received.

PRIMARY EMERGENCY CONTACTS

Campus Security emergency line: Extension 2000
Campus Security external number: +91 80000 02000
Campus medical centre: Extension 2010
Hostel duty supervisor: Extension 2401
Fire and evacuation control desk: Extension 2020
Facilities emergency desk: Extension 2030
Information Technology security incidents: Extension 2601

The external numbers and email domains in this synthetic document are for project testing and do not connect to real services.

IMMEDIATE THREAT TO LIFE OR SAFETY

Call Campus Security at extension 2000. Give the exact building, floor, room or nearby landmark. Follow the instructions of the responder and keep a safe distance from the hazard.

If national or local emergency services have already been contacted, inform Campus Security so that responders can be directed through the correct gate. Do not assume that another person has made the call.

MEDICAL EMERGENCY

Call the Campus Medical Centre at extension 2010 and Campus Security at extension 2000 when urgent transport or crowd control may be needed.

Do not move a seriously injured person unless the location is unsafe. Do not give medicine, food or drink unless instructed by a qualified responder. If trained, provide first aid within the limits of that training. Send another person to guide responders to the location.

FIRE, SMOKE OR BURNING SMELL

Activate the nearest fire alarm if it has not already sounded. Leave by the marked evacuation route and use stairs rather than lifts. Close doors behind you if this can be done without delay.

Call extension 2020 or Campus Security at extension 2000 from a safe location. Report the building, floor and visible conditions. Do not return for personal belongings and do not re-enter until an authorised responder declares the area safe.

SUSPICIOUS PACKAGE OR OBJECT

Do not touch, move, open or photograph the object at close range. Move away, discourage others from approaching and call Campus Security at extension 2000.

Do not use a radio or mobile telephone immediately beside a suspicious object. Follow the distance and evacuation instructions given by Campus Security.

THREATENING BEHAVIOUR OR VIOLENCE

Move to a safer location if possible and call extension 2000. Provide a description of the person, last known location, direction of movement and any visible weapon without placing yourself at further risk.

Do not confront or attempt to restrain the person unless immediate defensive action is unavoidable. Preserve relevant messages or records for authorised investigators.

MISSING OR AT-RISK STUDENT

For an immediate concern about a student's safety, contact Campus Security at extension 2000. Provide the student's name, student number if known, last confirmed location, time last seen, contact attempts and reason for concern.

A person does not need to wait for a fixed number of hours before reporting a credible safety concern. Routine inability to contact a classmate without a specific risk indicator may be reported through the non-emergency line at extension 2001.

HOSTEL EMERGENCY

Call the hostel duty supervisor at extension 2401 for an urgent residential incident and Campus Security at extension 2000 for a threat to life, fire, violence, forced entry or another serious safety matter.

Residents must keep corridors and exits clear and follow the instructions of the Warden, duty supervisor and emergency personnel. A maintenance request alone is not sufficient for an active electrical, water, fire or structural hazard.

ELECTRICAL HAZARD, WATER LEAK OR STRUCTURAL DAMAGE

Keep away from exposed wiring, standing water near electrical equipment, a damaged ceiling or another unstable area. Call Facilities Emergency at extension 2030 and notify Campus Security when people or access routes may be at risk.

Do not operate switches, touch damaged equipment or attempt a repair. If instructed to leave the area, warn nearby occupants without delaying your own evacuation.

GAS OR CHEMICAL ODOUR

Leave the immediate area without operating electrical switches or creating a flame. From a safe location, call Campus Security at extension 2000 and Facilities Emergency at extension 2030.

Provide the location and describe the smell, visible vapour, spill or container only from what can be observed safely. Do not attempt to identify or clean an unknown substance.

SEVERE WEATHER

Follow official alerts and move away from windows, trees, temporary structures and flooded areas as instructed. Do not enter water-covered roads or paths where the depth and electrical risk are unknown.

Classes or examinations are not cancelled solely because informal messages circulate. Closure, relocation and schedule decisions are communicated through official Institute channels.

CYBERSECURITY INCIDENT

For suspected account compromise, phishing that involved disclosure of credentials, unauthorised portal activity or loss of a device containing Institute information, call the IT security line at extension 2601.

Change the affected password from a trusted device when safe to do so. Do not delete suspicious messages or logs that may assist investigation. Never provide a one-time password to a person claiming to be support staff.

MENTAL HEALTH CRISIS

If a person appears to be in immediate danger of harming themselves or another person, stay at a safe distance, call Campus Security at extension 2000 and request medical assistance. Do not leave the person alone when it is safe to remain nearby.

For urgent but non-immediate support during service hours, contact the Student Wellness Centre at extension 2160. Email is not an emergency channel.

ACCESSIBILITY DURING AN EMERGENCY

Students who have an approved personal emergency assistance arrangement should follow that plan and notify responders of the accommodation required. Anyone who cannot use the normal evacuation route should move to the designated refuge area where one is provided and communicate their location.

OTHER STUDENTS must not carry or physically move a person unless instructed or immediate conditions make remaining in place more dangerous.

AFTER AN INCIDENT

Cooperate with safety instructions and preserve relevant records, photographs taken from a safe position, access logs or witness information. Do not publish identifying medical or personal information about affected people.

An incident report may be required after the immediate danger has passed. Submitting a report does not replace contacting emergency responders during an active incident.

DOCUMENT CONTROL

The Campus Safety Office maintains this document. Emergency numbers displayed at the incident location and live instructions from authorised responders take precedence over this directory. Report an incorrect or unreachable campus number to security.office@northbridge.example after immediate safety needs have been addressed.

STUDENT GRIEVANCE PROCEDURE 2026

Document ID: NIT-REG-GRV-2026
Issued by: Office of the Registrar
Published: 25 July 2026
Effective from: 1 August 2026
Version: 1.0

1. PURPOSE

This procedure provides a clear route for a student to raise a concern about an Institute service, administrative decision or failure to follow a published process. It is intended to support fair review, timely communication and a written outcome.

The procedure does not guarantee the result requested by the student. It ensures that the concern is sent to an appropriate office and considered under the applicable rules.

2. MATTERS COVERED

A grievance may concern an unreasonable delay, incorrect application of a published procedure, failure to provide an approved service, inaccurate administrative record, unfair treatment in an administrative process or another service-related action within the Institute's responsibility.

Examples include an unresolved registration record, failure to process a complete application within the published period, inconsistent application of a hostel procedure or an administrative decision that does not identify its policy basis.

3. MATTERS HANDLED UNDER OTHER PROCEDURES

The following matters should normally use their specialised procedure:

Academic grade disagreement or re-evaluation: Controller of Examinations procedure.
Attendance record correction: department verification and Academic Affairs process.
Disciplinary allegation or appeal: student discipline regulations.
Harassment or discrimination: equal opportunity and safeguarding procedure.
Scholarship selection review: scholarship policy and notified review route.
Employment complaint by a student employee: applicable employment procedure.
Immediate safety incident or suspected crime: Campus Security.

The Student Grievance Office will redirect a submission when another procedure clearly applies. Redirection is not a decision on the merits of the concern.

4. INFORMAL RESOLUTION

Where safe and reasonable, the student should first contact the office that provided the service or made the decision. The student should explain the problem, identify the requested correction and retain the correspondence or service reference.

The responsible office should normally reply within five working days. An informal enquiry is not required where the concern involves possible retaliation, a serious conflict of interest, sensitive misconduct or an immediate deadline that would make informal resolution ineffective.

5. FORMAL SUBMISSION

A formal grievance must be submitted through the student grievance portal using Form GRV-01. If the portal is unavailable, the Student Grievance Office may provide an accessible alternative.

The submission must include:

Student name and student number.
Institute email address and current programme.
The office, decision, service or event concerned.
Relevant dates and existing application or ticket references.
A clear description of what occurred.
Steps already taken to resolve the matter.
The outcome or correction requested.
Copies of relevant notices, correspondence or records.

Passwords, complete payment-card details and unrelated personal records must not be included.

6. SUBMISSION PERIOD

A grievance should be submitted within 20 working days after the student became aware of the matter. A later submission may be accepted when illness, delayed access to records, a continuing problem or another reasonable circumstance explains the delay.

The student should explain the reason for delay. Acceptance of a late grievance does not imply that the grievance will be upheld.

7. ACKNOWLEDGEMENT AND INITIAL REVIEW

The Student Grievance Office will normally acknowledge a formal submission within two working days and issue a case reference in the format GRV-2026-XXXXX.

The initial review checks whether the submission is understandable, within Institute responsibility and supported by enough information to begin review. The office may request missing records or redirect the case to a specialised procedure.

If additional information is requested, the student should provide it within five working days unless an extension is agreed. A case may be closed when essential information is not provided after a reminder.

8. REVIEW OFFICER

An officer who was not directly responsible for the disputed action will normally conduct the review. The officer may examine records, request a response from the responsible office and speak with the student or relevant employees.

The review officer must disclose a conflict of interest. When a reasonable conflict exists, the case will be reassigned.

9. INTERIM ACTION

Submitting a grievance does not automatically suspend a deadline, fee, examination decision, hostel action or other requirement. The student must request interim action separately and explain why it is necessary to prevent significant and irreversible harm.

The authorised office may approve, refuse or limit interim action. An interim arrangement does not determine the final outcome.

10. EXPECTED REVIEW PERIOD

A written outcome should normally be issued within 15 working days after the complete grievance is accepted for review. Complex cases may require additional time.

If the review cannot be completed within that period, the Student Grievance Office should inform the student of the reason and provide a revised expected date. Time spent waiting for information requested from the student may be excluded from the review period.

11. POSSIBLE OUTCOMES

The written outcome may:

Uphold the grievance in full or in part.
Decline the grievance with reasons.
Correct an administrative record.
Require an office to reconsider a decision under the correct procedure.
Provide a delayed service by a stated date.
Recommend a process improvement.
Refer a separate concern to another authorised procedure.

The outcome should identify the information considered, the applicable rule or process and any action to be taken. The grievance process cannot award a qualification, alter an academic grade outside the examination procedure or create an exception that the Institute has no authority to grant.

12. REQUEST FOR REVIEW

A student may request one review of the formal outcome within ten working days of receiving it. The request must use Form GRV-02 and identify at least one of the following grounds:

A material procedural error affected the outcome.
Relevant evidence was available but was not reasonably considered.
New evidence could not reasonably have been provided earlier.
The stated outcome is inconsistent with the policy identified in the decision.

Disagreement with the outcome alone is not a ground for review. The review officer may confirm the outcome, modify it or return the matter for reconsideration. The review decision completes the internal grievance procedure unless another regulation expressly provides a further route.

13. SUPPORT AND REPRESENTATION

A student may seek assistance from an approved student adviser or accessibility support person. The student remains responsible for the accuracy of the submission and should participate directly unless an approved accommodation provides otherwise.

The Institute may communicate with a representative only after receiving the student's written authorisation and verifying the representative's identity.

14. CONFIDENTIALITY AND RECORDS

Grievance information is shared only with people who need it to assess, respond to or administer the case, subject to law and Institute policy. Complete confidentiality cannot be promised when investigation or safety action requires disclosure.

Case records are retained under the Institute records schedule. Anonymous information may be used to identify recurring service problems.

15. PROTECTION FROM RETALIATION

A student must not be disadvantaged for raising a concern in good faith or participating honestly in a review. A report of suspected retaliation should quote the original case reference and be sent promptly to the Student Grievance Office.

Knowingly false statements, fabricated evidence or misuse of the procedure may be addressed under applicable regulations. A grievance that is not upheld is not, by itself, evidence of bad faith.

16. ACCESSIBILITY

Students who require an accessible format, communication support or an adjustment to participate in the procedure should contact the Accessibility Support Office or Student Grievance Office. An approved adjustment does not change the standard used to decide the grievance.

17. CONTACT

Student Grievance Office
Administration Building, Second Floor, Room A-215
Telephone: Extension 2150
Email: grievances@northbridge.example
Public service hours: Monday to Friday, 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

Emergency and immediate safety matters must be reported to Campus Security at extension 2000 rather than submitted only as a grievance.

18. DOCUMENT AUTHORITY

The Registrar maintains this procedure. A later dated Institute regulation or specialised appeal procedure takes precedence for a matter within its scope. Changes to forms or portal locations may be announced separately without changing the substantive review periods in this version.
